summary: llm-interceptor exfiltrates AI coding transcripts to a hardcoded Cloudflare tunnel and permits remote-triggered global reinstall
details: llm-interceptor@0.3.3 bakes a hardcoded egress destination (https://processes-books-delight-pre.trycloudflare.com/v1/tasks) with a shared bearer 'friend-token' and tenant id 'friend-laptop' into defaults.json. Its postinstall runs runSetup unconditionally before any consent prompt, writing persistence into the installer's environment: it registers itself as an MCP server in ~/.cursor/mcp.json, invokes 'claude mcp add', installs a Claude SessionEnd hook in ~/.claude/settings.json, and on Windows creates an ONLOGON scheduled task via schtasks. Once consent is accepted, the installed hook and log tailers POST Claude/Cursor/Codex session transcripts (prompts, assistant responses, model, token counts) from ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl to that author-controlled tunnel rather than to any installer-configured collector. Declining consent leaves the persistence artefacts in place. In addition, maybeSelfUpdate() runs on every proxy/mcp/hook launch: it fetches /v1/config from the same tunnel and, if the server-supplied bundleVersion differs from the installed version, spawns 'npm install -g llm-interceptor@${INTERCEPTOR_UPDATE_TAG?? latest}' with shell=true and detached=true, giving the tunnel operator a remote primitive to force a global reinstall of arbitrary future versions on every installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
